items.title: Homemaker’s household services cannot be ignored in accident compensation merely because she is over 70: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has held that while determining motor accident compensation, a homemaker’s unpaid household and caregiving services cannot be disregarded merely because she is above 70 years of age [Ganga Devi v Rajesh Kumar & Ors] . Justice Anish Dayal said that the assessment of compensation should not be founded upon stereotypes or assumptions that a person ceases to contribute merely by reason of having attained an advanced age. The Court warned against such prejudices and said that data demonstrates that women beyond the age of 70 years continue to render gratuitous services to their families, including household and caregiving services. “This Court is conscious that such contributions, particularly those rendered within the household and without monetary remuneration, are often overlooked or undervalued. However, the absence of a monetary consideration cannot operate to the advantage of the tortfeasor or diminish the compensation otherwise payable to the injured claimant,” the Bench ruled.
